name: EASA Part-IS.D.OR
full_name: EASA Part-IS.D.OR: Information security organisation requirements (Annex to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1645) for Part-21 design and production organisations, aerodrome operators and apron management service providers, and, from 27 March 2031, certain ground handling organisations
issuing_body: European Commission; European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA)

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1645 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 as regards requirements for the management of information security risks with a potential impact on aviation safety for organisations covered by Regulations (EU) No 748/2012 and (EU) No 139/2014 (consolidated text, CELEX 02022R1645-20251016)
sources.version: Consolidated version of 16 October 2025 (incorporating (EU) 2025/22 and corrigendum C1)
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex)

sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex)

scoring.summary: Part-IS has no official score. The compliance percentage is the share of applicable requirements assessed compliant; any non-compliance is a finding that needs a corrective action plan.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every applicable point of it is met.
Part-IS.D.OR applies from 16 October 2025.
Ground handling organisations that process third-party data or supply operational data to aircraft operators come into scope from 27 March 2031.

Applies to the organisations listed in Article 2(1): Part-21 design and production organisations (except those solely involved with ELA2 aircraft), and aerodrome operators and apron management service providers under Part-ADR.OR.
rules.quote: This Regulation applies to the following organisations:

rules.summary: The competent authority may approve an organisation not implementing IS.D.OR.200(a) to (d) and IS.D.OR.205 to IS.D.OR.260, based on a documented risk assessment showing no information security risk with a potential impact on aviation safety. Reporting under Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 and IS.D.OR.200(a)(13) still apply.
rules.quote: the organisation may be granted approval by the competent authority not to implement the requirements referred to in points (a) to (d)) and the related requirements contained in points IS.D.OR.205 through IS.D.OR.260

rules.summary: An IS.D.OR.200(e) approval is reviewed each oversight audit cycle and whenever the organisation's scope of work changes.
rules.quote: The continued validity of that approval will be reviewed by the competent authority following the applicable oversight audit cycle and whenever changes are implemented in the scope of work of the organisation.

rules.from: the time the condition has been known to the organisation
rules.summary: A significant information security incident or vulnerability must be notified to the competent authority (and, where applicable, the design approval holder or system designer) as soon as the organisation knows of it.
rules.quote: a notification shall be submitted to the competent authority and, if applicable, to the design approval holder or to the organisation responsible for the design of the system or constituent, as soon as the condition has been known to the organisation

rules.from: the time the condition has been known to the organisation
rules.summary: A full report must follow as soon as possible and within 72 hours of the organisation becoming aware, unless exceptional circumstances prevent it.
rules.quote: as soon as possible, but not exceeding 72 hours from the time the condition has been known to the organisation, unless exceptional circumstances prevent this

rules.timing: as soon as actions are identified
rules.summary: A follow-up report on recovery and prevention actions is due as soon as those actions have been identified.
rules.quote: The follow-up report shall be submitted as soon as those actions have been identified

rules.summary: For each finding notified by the competent authority the organisation identifies the root cause, defines a corrective action plan and demonstrates the correction to the authority's satisfaction.
Root-cause analysis, the corrective action plan and the demonstrated correction must be completed within the period agreed with the competent authority.
rules.quote: The actions referred to in point (a) shall be carried out within the period agreed with the competent authority.

rules.summary: The initial ISMM must be approved by the competent authority, which keeps a copy. Declaring organisations do not need approval.
rules.quote: The initial issue of the ISMM shall be approved and a copy shall be retained by the competent authority. An approval shall not be required for declaring organisations.

rules.summary: ISMM amendments outside the organisation's amendment procedure, and those linked to IS.D.OR.255(b) changes, need competent authority approval (not for declaring organisations).
rules.quote: Any amendments that are not included within the scope of this procedure and any amendments related to the changes referred to in point IS.D. OR.255(b), shall be approved by the competent authority.

rules.summary: The procedure for managing and notifying ISMS changes must be approved by the competent authority, except for declaring organisations.
rules.quote: This procedure shall be approved by the competent authority, except for declaring organisations.

rules.summary: ISMS changes outside the approved procedure need an application before the change and formal approval before implementation; declaring organisations may implement immediately.
rules.quote: the change shall be implemented only upon receipt of a formal approval by the competent authority, except for declaring organisations, which may implement the change immediately

rules.timing: organisation-defined calendar or after an incident
rules.summary: ISMS effectiveness and maturity must be assessed on a calendar the organisation predefines, and after any information security incident.
rules.quote: That assessment shall be carried out on a calendar basis predefined by the organisation or following an information security incident.

rules.summary: Any IS.D.OR.200(e) approval and its risk assessment are kept at least 5 years after the approval loses validity.
rules.quote: shall be retained at least until 5 years after the approval has lost its validity

rules.from: the contract being amended or terminated
rules.summary: Contracts for information security management activities are kept at least 5 years after amendment or termination.
rules.quote: shall be retained at least until 5 years after the contract has been amended or terminated

rules.summary: Records of key processes, identified risks and treatments, and reported incidents and vulnerabilities are kept at least 5 years.
rules.quote: The records referred to in point (1)(iii), (iv) and (v) shall be retained at least for a period of 5 years.

rules.summary: Qualification and experience records of information security staff are kept while they work there and at least 3 years after they leave.
rules.quote: records be retained for as long as the person works for the organisation, and for at least 3 years after the person has left the organisation

glossary.definition: European Union Aviation Safety Agency, which issues the acceptable means of compliance and guidance material for Part-IS.
The EU aviation information security rules: organisation requirements in Regulation (EU) 2023/203 (Part-IS.D.OR) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1645 (Part-IS.D.OR).
Information security management system: the processes, procedures, roles and responsibilities an organisation uses to manage information security risks with a potential impact on aviation safety.
Information security management manual: the document that describes the organisation's ISMS and is made available to the competent authority.
Acceptable means of compliance: EASA's non-binding standards by which an organisation can show it meets a requirement.
Guidance material: EASA's non-binding material that explains a requirement or its AMC.
Annex I to Regulation (EU) No 748/2012: certification of aircraft and related products, and approval of design and production organisations.
European Light Aircraft 2: a defined class of light aeroplanes, sailplanes, balloons and airships (Regulation (EU) No 748/2012, Article 1(2)(j)).
Apron management services, regulated with aerodromes under Part-ADR.OR.
